issue.title: tests: three guarantees lost their tests when Cursor's built-in was retired (#541, #1147, #1789)
issue.body:
Retiring Cursor's built-in (the retire stack pushed with this issue's number in its body) removed three tests whose fake was the built-in's `cursor-agent`:

- `TestFetchNewWaitsForASlowSignIn` (#1789): FetchNew waits for a CLI asked who is signed in for the first time that answers after a look's wait.
- `TestFetchNewListsAgainForAnAnswerWhileListing` (#1147): a CLI that answers while the accounts are listed has its account listed in the same pass.
- `TestProvidersAnswerWhileListsComeIn` (#541, internal/gui/providers_fetching_unix_test.go): the Providers page answers while an account's list comes in.

The code they guard still runs. `cliIdentities()` (internal/provider/cli_identity.go) still holds `cursorStatus`. `fetchNewHeld` (models.go) still calls `awaitIdentities`. `cursorIdentity()` feeds the Cursor plugin's carried-over account (plugin_accounts.go) and the mover (migrate_side.go). So #1789 and #1147 can still regress, for the Cursor plugin's account, and nothing would go red.

To do: re-home the two provider tests onto the Cursor plugin's account, with a fake `cursor-agent about` that answers late, and the GUI one onto an HTTP-listed account (Antigravity or Copilot) with a slow fake vendor.

comments.body:
Where the items from this list stand after the retire stack (0f1666b38..de671719a):

- #1789: the check is re-homed on Codex in the TUI. It no longer depends on a retired built-in.
- #1147 and #2390: no longer apply. 0718beb43 removed the CLI identity wait those tests were about.
- #541: its GUI test is still to do, so this stays open for that.

The page's own guard was lost with Cursor's built-in: e405315d deleted `internal/gui/providers_fetching_unix_test.go`, whose fake was `cursor-agent`, and nothing took over the path `providersState` still runs (`internal/gui/providers.go`: `FetchNewBehind` before the accounts are listed, `FetchingNew` into `providersJSON.Fetching`). `TestFetchingNewOnceStarted` holds the provider side in `internal/provider`; the page's side was unheld.

This branch re-homes it as `TestProvidersAnswerWhileListsComeIn` in `internal/gui/providers_fetching_test.go`: Codex is signed in under the test's own home, `provider.CodexBase` points at an httptest vendor that holds its answer until the test releases it, and `/api/providers` is asked while that answer is outstanding. The page must answer with `fetching` set and the account's list still in flight, then list the vendor's model once the answer is released.

The issue suggested Antigravity or Copilot. Neither vendor's list endpoint can be pointed elsewhere from `internal/gui` today (`codeAssistDaily` and `copilotGHEOrigin` are unexported, and an Antigravity account also needs a Google login made), while Codex's endpoint is the one the gui tests already redirect, so the page's guarantee is held against a Codex account. Say if you would rather see a test seam added for one of the two instead.

[fix/2621-tests-three-guarantees-lost-their](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/2621-tests-three-guarantees-lost-their), commit b66100d6080ca66ddfcfb326f654e03ecdc88277 (base `dc1cfe01`).

What was run: `gofmt -l` on the changed file (nothing), `go build ./...` (nothing), `go vet ./internal/gui/` (nothing), `go test ./internal/gui/ -run '^TestProvidersAnswerWhileListsComeIn$' -count=2 -race` (ok), `go test ./internal/gui/ -count=1 -timeout 20m` (ok, 461 tests). The test passes on the unchanged product code, since the behavior was never broken, only its guard lost. It goes red when the page is made to wait (`FetchNew` in place of `FetchNewBehind`: "0 lists in flight when the page answered") and when the page stops saying a list is on its way (`Fetching` set false: "not told the lists are on their way").

This is a fork branch, ready for review; it makes no claim on the issue's ownership.
